Subject: Throughput commitment proposal for HelioEdge - tokens/sec vs p95 SLO

Hi Alex / HelioEdge procurement team,

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, we want to put a concrete sizing proposal on the table so procurement and engineering can validate the Dedicated commitment. To make sure we're aligned, below is what we captured for production traffic patterns and the high-level ask:

- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 400 ms for interactive chat flows.
- Traffic mix (customer-provided): short completions ~70%, medium ~20%, long/generative ~10% (details requested below).
- Peak concurrent sessions: you mentioned spikes to ~200-300 active requests during launches.

Action: Can you confirm the typical response token lengths and whether those spikes are 1) short bursts lasting minutes or 2) sustained for hours? That will change our recommended slab sizing.

I attached an initial sizing sheet (helioedge_initial_sizing_sheet.csv) that maps several traffic scenarios to tokens/sec and GPU counts. Ben and Laura from my team are looped for a quick engineering sanity check — any obvious gaps we'll flag before an offer.

Proposed next step: if you confirm token lengths and peak shape, we’ll respond with a recommended Dedicated slab (GPU count + fallback policy) and an estimated unit price for committed capacity.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Throughput commitment proposal for HelioEdge - tokens/sec vs p95 SLO

Hey Soojin,

Thanks for the follow-up. Confirming the breakdown:
- Short chat completions (70%): avg 220 tokens per response, typically single-turn quick answers.
- Medium flows (20%): avg 900 tokens, multi-turn assistance (2-3 messages).
- Long generative workloads (10%): avg 2,800 tokens, often triggered by a small cohort of power users.

Peak behavior: launch spikes are sharp — 10-30 minutes at peak, but we also have predictable daily peaks ~2 hours long during US business hours. Typical burst concurrency at peak: ~250 active requests, baseline concurrency ~35-50.

We really need a firm p95 <= 400 ms for the short/medium flows — long generative jobs can be best-effort (we accept higher latency there). Also please include any cost/price guidance tied to committed GPUs and what fallback looks like if Dedicated capacity saturates.

Alex Chen
Head of Platform, HelioEdge
alex@helioedge.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:08:00Z
Subject: Fwd: HelioEdge traffic detail + ask — quick sizing recommendation (internal)

Team,

Forwarding Alex's traffic breakdown. Key asks: p95 <= 400ms for short/medium flows, expected peak conc ~250 for up to ~30 minutes and long tails of ~2 hours daily. They accept degraded service for long jobs but want interactive flows preserved.

My back-of-envelope on tokens/sec at peak (using their averages):
- Weighted avg tokens per response = 0.7*220 + 0.2*900 + 0.1*2800 = 154 + 180 + 280 = 614 tokens/response.
- If peak concurrent active requests = 250 and target p95 = 0.4s, required aggregate throughput ~= 250 * 614 / 0.4 = 383,750 tokens/sec.

Sizing assumptions to sanity-check:
- We should assume batching and KV-cache effectiveness for short flows reduces per-request cost; however interactive p95 target limits batching window (< 40ms).
- We should size against sustained 2-hour peak and add a 1.5x safety buffer for headroom and planned model updates.
- Engineering thumb rule: use conservative per-GPU sustained throughput = 28,000 tokens/sec for their primary chat model (with optimized kernels + q4f16 on T4/A10 equivalents). This accounts for mixed sequence lengths and warm KV caches.

Using those numbers:
- Baseline GPUs = ceil(383,750 / 28,000) = 14 GPUs.
- With 1.5x safety buffer => recommend 21 GPUs reserved for Dedicated slab during launch windows.

Questions for engineering: is 28k/gpu a reasonable conservative sustained rate for their mixture? Also, we need a fallback plan: recommend hybrid routing where 90% of short/medium requests use Dedicated, and overflow routes to Hosted API with priority throttling and token-based cost sharing.

I've attached the initial sizing sheet and a short note for procurement (helioedge_requirements_packet.pdf). Please flag anything that seems off or add model-specific per-GPU throughputs if you have better numbers.

Thanks — Soojin

Attachment: helioedge_requirements_packet.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T14:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelioEdge traffic detail + ask — quick sizing recommendation (internal)

Sooj, Laura, Rachel — quick check from infra side. Numbers look directionally sound; a few notes and adjustments:

1) Per-GPU throughput: 28k tokens/sec is reasonable for a quantized 13B-style chat model on an A10 / v4 equivalent if we are careful on kernel selection and sequence-caching. For mixed workloads we should assume degradation during long-gen spikes — e.g., long requests can temporarily reduce effective throughput to ~18k/gpu if many occupy KV caches.

2) Warm-up and KV cache: For interactive p95 we need a warm KV cache slice and pre-warmed model instances. That increases memory pressure but preserves p95 for short flows. Plan to reserve ~10% of the slab as pre-warmed instances (not counted for concurrency). So of 21 GPUs, expect ~2 GPUs effectively reserved for warm pools.

3) Autoscaling and fallback: Recommend a two-tier Dedicated slab: primary reserved pool 14 GPUs (committed, covers baseline peak) + burst pool 7 GPUs (pre-paid but throttled) + overflow to Hosted. Configure smart routing: route by request size and SLA tag (short/medium go to Dedicated first).

4) Cost note for commercial: with our current pricing bands, committed 14 GPUs + 7 burst reserved for the year maps to the pricing band we discussed — I’ll follow up with procurement on exact numbers once procurement confirms contract term.

Action items: Laura to validate the 28k/18k per-gpu figures against the kernel matrix; Rachel to draft an explicit SLA fallback clause describing routing + cost apportionment.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed Dedicated slab and fallback plan for HelioEdge — next steps

Alex / HelioEdge team,

Thanks for the details — we've scoped a recommended Dedicated offer based on your traffic profile and the SLO target. Summary below:

Proposal (conservative):
- Committed Dedicated slab: 14 GPUs (primary pool) — sized to cover the baseline peak with p95 <= 400ms for short/medium flows.
- Burst reserved pool: +7 GPUs (hot standby) — available for scheduled launches and sustained 2-hour peaks; burst usage subject to a higher unit rate.
- Headroom policy: we recommend a 1.5x safety buffer for onboarding launches (21 GPUs total during high-peak windows).
- Warm pool: reserve ~10% of primary pool for pre-warmed instances to preserve p95 for interactive flows.

Routing & fallback:
- Short/medium flows: primary routing to Dedicated with a 40ms batching window goal; if Dedicated utilization exceeds 90% for >60s, overflow routes to Hosted API with request tagging and cost apportionment.
- Long generative jobs: best-effort on Dedicated; can be queued or spilled to Hosted during peaks.

Estimated capacity math we used (included in attached sizing sheet):
- Weighted avg tokens/response = 614 tokens
- Required aggregate throughput at 250 conc and 0.4s p95 = ~384k tokens/sec
- Conservative per-GPU sustained throughput = 28k tokens/sec => baseline 14 GPUs; 1.5x buffer => 21 GPUs.

Next steps:
1) Alex — confirm whether you prefer a single committed slab with scheduled burst windows or a two-pool pricing model (primary + burst). Your procurement feedback will drive pricing.
2) Ben/Laura/Rachel — finalize per-GPU throughput numbers and draft SLA fallback text.
3) I will prepare a commercial term sheet (commit period, burst pricing tiers) once procurement confirms preference.

If this looks good, can we schedule a 30-min call early next week to lock down procurement preferences and the final GPU counts?

Best,
SoJin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
